highlights.title: Apple announces September iPhone launch event
highlights.summary: Apple's next launch event will take place on September 9th at 1PM ET. Invites to the event, which has a "Surprise and shine" tagline, were sent out on Wednesday. The event will take place at the Steve Jobs Theater in Apple Park, but there will also be a livestream on Apple's website.
body: September’s show could be a big one, as Apple may finally announce the long-rumored foldable iPhone. A photo of an apparent dummy unit indicates the foldable may have a wide form factor that’s similar to what Samsung used with the Galaxy Z Fold 8, a phone that our reviewer Dominic Preston said “feels like the future.”

Apple is also expected to refresh its Pro and Pro Max phones, but those are rumored to be iterative upgrades and not a big redesign like Apple announced last year. Should past trends continue, they’ll likely be called the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max.

However Apple reportedly won’t announce the base model iPhone 18 at the event and instead introduce it next year. In 2027, Apple is also rumored to be launching an iPhone 18e and a second-generation iPhone Air.
This event will also be the first with John Ternus as Apple’s CEO. Formerly the company’s hardware chief, Ternus is set to take over from Tim Cook on September 1st.

highlights.title: FIA confirms Mercedes granted engine upgrades despite Red Bull complaints
highlights.summary: The FIA has confirmed that Mercedes have been granted the opportunity to make upgrades to their engine despite protestations from rival teams.
body: Following the introduction of all-new engines for the 2026 season, Formula 1's governing body implemented an Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) system, designed to allow manufacturers to catch up to the performance of the leading power unit during the rules cycle.

It was revealed in June after the first round of performance assessment, which included the first five rounds of the season, that the FIA had adjudged Red Bull to have the strongest engine and had granted upgrades to Mercedes, Ferrari, Audi and Honda.
The FIA never revealed their findings to the media, but teams and drivers confirmed the outcome publicly, while a document revealing the results was also leaked.

The ruling was seen as controversial because the consensus in the paddock was that Mercedes, whose works team had won the first six grands prix of the season, were being given an upgrade, while Red Bull, who had managed just a single podium in that time, would potentially lose more ground to their rivals.

highlights.title: Bill Gates is deeply worried about AI, and he’s no longer staying quiet
highlights.summary: Bill Gates has been reflecting a lot on AI lately, and the process has triggered a stark awakening. Once a staunch AI optimist, the Microsoft cofounder is now deeply pessimistic about what AI means for our collective future.
body: Microsoft’s cofounder used to be optimistic about AI, now he’s concerned it could be ‘the worst source of injustice.’

Having been conspicuously quiet on AI issues recently, Gates is back with a nearly 6,000-word essay seeking to reclaim a central role in shaping the technology globally. Titled “The turbulent AI era is here. The choices we make now are critical,” Gates warns the world is not remotely ready for what is coming. Worse still, he notes, “we are not preparing for it.”

Gates attempts to chart a path forward, but the essay largely treads familiar ground, identifying deeply entrenched, systemic hurdles familiar in matters of global governance while offering little in the way of novel solutions. The result is a bleak departure from the hopeful excitement about AI present in the billionaire’s 2023 essay on the matter, though Gates insists it is not too late “to ensure that the good outweighs the bad.”

highlights.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's Beta Will Be Playable on Switch 2 for Free This Weekend
highlights.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 will be playable on Nintendo Switch 2 for free this weekend. Starting Friday, August 28 at 10 AM PDT, Nintendo Switch 2 players will have the opportunity to try Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 for free.
body: The Switch 2 version will boast unique features such as gyro controls, Joy-Con mouse controls, and, of course, being able to play the game on a handheld. Additionally, Switch 2 players will get free access to the game's Vault Edition content during the beta. This includes access to special skins, weapon blueprints, and more. Players can pre-load the beta on Switch 2 right now and pre-order the full game.

It's the first time a Call of Duty game has been on a Nintendo platform since Call of Duty: Ghosts on Wii U. Nintendo fans have been wanting to see the franchise return to Nintendo hardware since then, but it hasn't been feasible until now. Digital Legends are developing the game's Switch 2 version after having helped develop Call of Duty: Warzone Mobile before its cancelation. The studio also did support work on the last two Black Ops games.

The company apologised for the delays in releasing official updates on the highly anticipated title, but vowed to "exceed" fans' expectations in a special preview airing on Netflix this week.

highlights.title: My mum has died – and there is one kind of response I can’t stand | Polly Hudson
highlights.summary: The platitudes, euphemisms and cliches are excruciating. But the people who say nothing at all are the worst. Luckily, I already knew having a comic thought at a tragic moment is a natural stress response, or I might have worried.
body: In Curb Your Enthusiasm, when Marty Funkhouser’s mother’s wheelchair was run over by a car, he proclaimed himself an orphan. David informed him he was too old to be an orphan. Funkhouser insisted that if your parents are dead, you’re an orphan.

Images of Annie-like red curls aside, the people who brought you into the world both having left it is pretty profound. I’m lucky to have a lot of support, but it’s a hard knock in life. A singularly specific brand of aloneness; the natural order that feels anything but. It’s so weird. There’s no one to tell me off any more, either. I wonder what I may get up to. What if I fall in with a bad crowd?

My mum “had a good innings though”, as I have been reminded roughly thrice daily. It’s been 14 years since my dad died, and there’s so much I’d forgotten about the grief game – namely the platitudes, the strange language, and how terrible so many of us are at dealing with it. The best reaction so far was a bloke who replied to my breaking of the news for sadmin purposes with: “OK, that’s fine.” At least he gave me a good story.

highlights.title: AI Slop Is Ruining Cute Animals on the Internet
highlights.summary: Pet owners, rescue agencies, and wildlife groups are calling for new safeguards as AI makes it harder to tell whether animals, from polar bears to house cats, are real or fake.
body: AI-generated videos and pictures are destroying one of the largest and most enduring sources of joy and compassion on the internet: animals. Whether the imagery features sailors rescuing a polar bear, baby cows separated from their mothers, or a lost pet that was miraculously found, many people have reached the point where they can’t take the creatures on their feeds at face value anymore. The explosion of deepfakes and AI slop over the past few years has led to widespread frustration among viewers, creators, and organizations that support animals, forcing everyone to hunt in the pixels for glitches or other telltale signs of AI.

Mibbby Butler was overjoyed one day in April when she received a text message that her lost cat, Brooklyn, had supposedly been found. Her roommate’s boyfriend had allegedly taken the cat and dumped him 30 minutes away in the Los Angeles suburbs the day prior. Butler quickly posted a missing poster on social media, and she was driving around with her roommate searching for Brooklyn when a stranger sent her a photo. In it, he is sitting on a kitchen counter while being embraced by a girl.

highlights.title: Solheim Cup captain Nordqvist announces shock mid-season retirement
highlights.summary: Solheim Cup captain Anna Nordqvist has announced via social media that she will retire from playing professional golf after this week's FM Championship, live on Sky Sports.
body: The three-time major winner will captain Team Europe at Bernardus Golf from September 11-13, having featured in each of the previous nine Solheim Cups as a player and been part of five winning teams.

Nordqvist has been a playing vice-captain in the last two contests but quickly ruled herself out of juggling captaincy with playing against Team USA in the Netherlands, despite still regularly featuring on the LPGA Tour and impressing in the majors.

The 39-year-old remains inside the world's top 120 and sits in the top 75 on the Race to CME Globe standings, although has now confirmed her intention to call time on her glittering playing career before the end of the LPGA Tour season.
In a post shared by the LPGA Tour and Ladies European Tour, Nordqvist said: "It's with a grateful heart I am retiring from playing professional golf in Boston this week."

highlights.title: Video Game Icon Tim Curry Dies at 80
highlights.summary: Tim Curry, the beloved English actor who played iconic and eccentric roles like the scientist Dr. Frank-N-Furter in The Rocky Horror Picture Show, the harried butler Wadsworth in Clue, and Pennywise the Clown in the original adaptation of Stephen King’s It, has died. He was 80 years old.
body: TMZ was first to report Curry's death. The actor reportedly died Tuesday at his Los Angeles home. Curry suffered a major stroke in 2012 that affected his mobility and memory, though he continued to perform in voice roles and in special appearances. He voiced Chancellor Palpatine/Darth Sidious in the animated series Star Wars: The Clone Wars.

Curry's acting career started on the stage. He originally portrayed Dr. Frank-N-Furter in The Rocky Horror Show in London and on Broadway. He reprised the role in the 1975 film version of that musical, The Rocky Horror Picture Show, which was a modest success at release but went on to be an enduring cult hit, ultimately grossing more than $170 million at the box office.

In the 1980s, Curry achieved mainstream stardom in films such as the musical Annie, Ridley Scott's fantasy film Legend, and the board game adaptation whodunnit Clue. Later, Curry starred in memorable roles in The Hunt for Red October, the superhero film The Shadow, Muppet Treasure Island, and Congo.

highlights.title: Court blocks Trump FCC order that could flood broadcast TV with more election ads
highlights.summary: A federal appeals court yesterday blocked a Trump administration decision that could have resulted in even more political advertisements appearing on broadcast television during the upcoming elections.
body: The Federal Communications Commission recently ordered broadcasters to offer the lowest advertising rates to political parties and joint fundraising committees. Four Democratic candidates challenged the decision in court, saying that only individual candidates are entitled under US law to receive what is called the “lowest unit charge,” or LUC.

In a 2-1 vote, a judges’ panel at the US Court of Appeals for the 4th Circuit agreed with the candidates and set aside the FCC decision that was scheduled to take effect on September 4. That’s the start date of the 60-day period before the election in which broadcasters must offer the lowest ad rates to qualified candidates.

“There is no question that candidates are entitled to the LUC,” the ruling said. “But it is disputed whether political parties and joint fundraising committees with non-candidate members can also be entitled to the LUC.”

The FCC Media Bureau asserted in a March 30 public notice that parties and authorized committees designated by candidates can get the discounts. The National Republican Congressional Committee and National Republican Senatorial Committee supported the FCC’s position during the court case.

highlights.title: Radar makes podcasts searchable — and usable by AI agents
highlights.summary: Particle’s new podcast intelligence platform transcribes and analyzes more than 130,000 podcasts, making their conversations searchable on the web and accessible to AI agents through an API and MCP.
body: Particle, the AI newsreader startup founded by former Twitter engineers, is shifting its focus to a potentially more lucrative idea: indexing the spoken conversations buried in podcasts and making them discoverable. On Wednesday, the company introduced Radar, a podcast search engine that not only transcribes podcast audio but also understands what it means, enabling it to pull out key quotes and highlights.
The solution has business potential, as it’s already attracted interest from hedge funds looking for data that their agents can’t see, explains Particle co-founder and CEO Sara Beykpour.

The idea itself stemmed from one of the Particle news-reading app’s most beloved features. The app had used an API to source interesting podcast clips that it then included alongside related news stories in the app’s feed.

Particle’s team realized the product’s value, but also that it was somewhat trapped in the news reader. As the movement around AI agents began to gain steam, the company decided to pivot and focus on building an API for its podcast intelligence product.

highlights.title: Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy Feels More Like a Tomb Raider Game
highlights.summary: There is nary a single rat in Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy, a new installment that acts as a prequel to the 14th-century series. While it carries the Plague Tale name, so much of the design ethos that makes up the experience bears little resemblance to anything in either Innocence or Requiem.
body: If you were to ask the average gamer what they knew about the Plague Tale series, you'd probably get a one-word answer: rats. Asobo Studio successfully carved out a niche with its Plague Tale duology, consisting of 2019's Innocence and 2022's Requiem, by rooting the series in a compelling set of design pillars. They featured stealth-focused combat, contained emotional storytelling, and — most importantly — gave you the ability to control writhing hordes of murderous rats. With the latest entry in the series, Asobo asks how many of those core pillars it can throw out while still feeling like a Plague Tale game.

highlights.title: My First Interview With Dolly Parton: Coming Face to Face With the Country Queen Who Soundtracked My Life
highlights.summary: I am sitting on a couch in a hotel suite in midtown Manhattan. I have two tape recorders on the coffee table ready to document my interview with one of my idols. I hear someone whistling from behind French doors. It’s not just any person whose whistle I hear. It’s Dolly Parton and she is
body: There she is – Dolly Parton. She’s wearing a pink cashmere sweater and a pink tweed miniskirt. Her heels are high as her hair.

I stand up and extend my hand. But Parton apparently isn’t a handshake kind of gal. She leans in for a hug. She smells like candy. As we separate, I let out a small breath. Parton looks at me and smiles, letting me know that I have nothing to be nervous about. I smile back and we settle into the couch, sitting side-by-side and chatting for the next hour or so.
It was 2001. I was there to interview Parton for US Weekly for the launch of her 37 th studio album and the second of her three bluegrass albums, “Little Sparrow.”
It would be the first of many interviews I had with Parton over the next couple of decades.

highlights.title: Volvo’s cars will warn one another about hazards in the road
highlights.summary: Volvo is updating three of its electric vehicles with new hazard alerts to warn drivers when there are animals or vulnerable road users ahead. The new connected safety features are based on Volvo's cars talking to one another, as opposed to crowdsourced alert systems used by popular navigation…
body: The company’s connected safety alerts will now warn drivers when there are animals, pedestrians, cyclists, roadwork, or accidents ahead.

The alerts work by using connected vehicle data from Volvo’s fleet of passenger vehicles in Europe, the US, and Canada. The car’s sensors and cameras are tuned to identify certain risks on the road. When one Volvo spots a hazard, it automatically logs the location and sends it to Volvo’s servers. Alerts are then sent to all other Volvo vehicles traveling along that same road. The alerts still depend on the car being connected to the cloud and the road existing in the map database, but Volvo’s newer EVs have plenty of computing power to handle the real-time processing requests.

Volvo said it’s updating its EVs with alerts for four types of hazards: large animals; vulnerable road users, like pedestrians or cyclists; roadwork; and accidents. The new alerts are coming to the Volvo EX90, ES90, and EX60. Volvo says it has 1 million vehicles on the road today with connected safety alert capabilities. And it shares its alert data with traffic management centers, as well as other vehicle brands, so its not just Volvo branded vehicles that are benefiting.

highlights.title: Raised on AI
highlights.summary: When my oldest child was born, I immediately set up Gmail and Twitter accounts in her name. I broadly announced her birth online and proceeded to plaster her photo across all sorts of platforms. In short, I began creating her digital footprint long before she could stand on her own two feet.
body: Fast-forward a couple of years to when my second kid came, and I had essentially the opposite reaction. I wanted to make sure I preserved her privacy. I didn’t want her birthday to be a matter of public record or her face to feed the algorithms. In time, I would go back and scrub much of the early footprint I had created for my first child as well.

What happened? I watched the promise of the early internet give way to the reality of its potential for abuse. I myself was already fully in the throes of smartphone and social media obsession. My wife, a pediatric nurse, grew increasingly alarmed at the number of children admitted to her hospital struggling with the effects of things like body dysmorphia or cyberbullying as a result of interactions on social media. We became those parents. The ones whose kids carry flip phones and aren’t on TikTok.
points: When my oldest child was born, I immediately set up Gmail and Twitter accounts in her name.
I broadly announced her birth online and proceeded to plaster her photo across all sorts of platforms.
In short, I began creating her digital footprint long before she could stand on her own two feet.
Fast-forward a couple of years to when my second kid came, and I had essentially the opposite reaction.

highlights.title: “We killed Clash Royale!”: What Supercell learned from failed updates
highlights.summary: Clash Royale has had its ups and downs over the years with some major backlash from players and fans over updates. During a session at Gamescom Dev titled 'Clash Royale: Lessons from the players', Supercell game design lead James Back and community manager Emilia Russell shared their insights from…
body: Russell noted, though, that even the harshest and most critical feedback comes from a place of caring about a game and players wanting the best for it - even if it’s not always given in the most clear or constructive way.

First, they opened up on the Season Shop. Described as “one of the most popular reward systems in the game”, it allowed players to spend Season Tokens on cards and other items. In March 2025, Supercell decided to remove it.

Back said it was for good reason. The team felt it only benefitted a small group of core players and they wanted to put the rewards somewhere more accessible to more players. The update worked at achieving that goal. The percentage of monthly active users earning any common wild cards grew from 59.8% in March 2025 to 67.4% in April 2025.
But due to the Season Shop’s popularity, its sudden removal resulted in “broken trust” and negative sentiment. The average daily rating on Google Play plummeted.

highlights.title: Telluride’s Julie Huntsinger on Her 20 Years Leading the Festival, Chasing ‘Digger’ and ‘Dune 3’ and a ‘True TBA’ Film Hidden Until Patrons Walk Into the Theater
highlights.summary: Julie Huntsinger has spent two decades as the guardian of the Telluride Film Festival — a jewel box of off-duty movie stars and power players relaxing in the mountains and a consequential launchpad for the fall awards season. As festival director, Huntsinger has her hallmarks.
body: Huntsinger sits down with Variety to discuss secret negotiations, the ones that got away and why she calls herself a “midwife.”

In some ways it’s changed a lot, and in others I recognize it completely. We’re in this old, pretty dilapidated building — maybe I shouldn’t use that word — and we joke that we hold it together with bubble gum and rubber bands. Marlow Stern called us “small but mighty” some years ago, and that’s right. We put it together with a huge amount of goodwill. That’s part of the miracle business. But the traditions — the secrecy of the program, the little rituals — are so beloved that when I came back I felt it was important to safeguard all of that.

People imagine we watch movies and go, “OK, we’ll take that one.” It starts out that way, and sometimes distributors and producers want a sense of what we think. I’ve had people say outright, “We’re not sure what we want to do with this movie, but we’d love your input.” Other times we really [want] something, and they say, “We know you like it, but we still want to go next year.”

highlights.title: Stuck bundts? You need ‘cake goop’: Natalie Paull’s lime and yoghurt bundt – recipe
highlights.summary: The cookbook author and owner of Melbourne’s Beatrix Bakes shares a her ‘100% reliable’ formula for freeing bundts from tins. When all the layer cakes are baked and iced, I will always love a slice of pretty patterned bundt.
body: Cake goop – a mix of flour, oil and butter – is a gift of guaranteed cake release that I found on the internet, and it means no more stuck bundts. Bless the baker who invented it! Goop has it all – release, plus enough sticking power to hold the batter as it rises and cools, without slumping. Additionally, mixing the flour with oil means you don’t get that fine, white, dusty crust on the outside of the cooked cake. Goop is 100% reliable with a 100% untarnished release record in my kitchen.

If you do have a small stuck piece of cake, shimmy it out of the tin with an offset spatula and patch it back on to the cake while warm. Pretty easy! If a whole ring of cake has stuck, cut it into workable sections, prise each out and place back on the cake. Drench the bundt with icing sugar after its soak to hide the Franken-bundt’s monster appearance.

The recipe calls for the eggs to be warmed before cracking. Warmer-than-room- temperature eggs emulsify into the creamed base better, and an emulsified mix means no “curdled” appearance. To do this, submerge the uncracked eggs in hot tap water for five minutes.

highlights.title: Researchers get two genetic codes to work at the same time
highlights.summary: The genetic code is what life everywhere uses to convert the information contained in DNA into specific protein sequences. With minor variations, the same genetic code is used by every living thing on Earth, suggesting it was already present in the last common ancestor of all of them.
body: Nevertheless, some preliminary steps have been taken. Researchers have managed to add some new amino acids to a bacterial cell and were able to make proteins that were one amino acid less than usual. But it’s a slog; for some of this work, people have had to re-engineer every single gene in a bacterial genome.

Now, researchers have found a way to operate two separate genetic codes simultaneously, avoiding the need to do any work to compensate for altering the code that every protein in a cell relies on. They didn’t test it in an actual cell, and it might cause some problems there. But it’s a creative solution that should accelerate some synthetic biology work.

To understand how this works, we need to go back to that high school biology class you might not have paid much attention to. In the genome, part of most genes is dedicated to encoding a protein. The linear arrangement of bases in the DNA gets directly translated into the linear sequence of amino acids that make up a protein. Each set of three bases in the DNA corresponds to a specific amino acid (with three exceptions, each of which signals the end of the protein).
points: The genetic code is what life everywhere uses to convert the information contained in DNA into specific protein sequences.
With minor variations, the same genetic code is used by every living thing on Earth, suggesting it was already present in the last common ancestor of all of them.

highlights.title: AI helps design new materials that work in the real world
highlights.summary: The “CrysVCD” tool developed at MIT could cut the huge amounts of time and money spent on screening out chemically unstable designs.
body: Today, anyone with a large enough artificial intelligence model can generate millions of new material designs in minutes. Unfortunately, that hasn’t led to a huge leap in the number of new materials being used to improve the performance of products like computer chips and rockets.

One reason for the translation gap is that current models don’t reliably factor in the chemical stability of the materials they generate, and unstable materials aren’t very useful in the real world. That forces industries to allocate huge computational budgets to screening out all the unstable materials they generate, in some cases leaving behind a tiny fraction of usable options.

Now, MIT researchers have developed a framework that can be applied at the beginning of the materials generation process to vastly improve the stability rate while achieving targeted material properties. It works by ensuring every design satisfies certain key rules of chemistry relating to the electrons around the materials’ atoms before the expensive generation step begins. The researchers call their approach “crystal generator with valence-constrained design, or CrysVCD.
points: The “CrysVCD” tool developed at MIT could cut the huge amounts of time and money spent on screening out chemically unstable designs.

highlights.title: I've Tried Star Wars Zero Company on Five Different PCs, and It's Been a Nightmare
highlights.summary: We got off to such a great start this year, with a ton of PC games that looked great and still ran well on pretty much any hardware. One of the common themes among games like Crimson Desert, Resident Evil Requiem, and Forza Horizon 6 was that none of them were running on Unreal Engine 5.
body: I've spent about five hours in Zero Company so far, and while that means I'm still pretty early in the otherwise fantastic game, I've still run into more than my fair share of technical issues, across all types of hardware. When the game isn't bugging out in some way, I've been having a blast with it, and it's important to note that our reviewer Dan Stapleton hasn't had nearly the same depth of issues that I've had.
What's funny is that the technical problems are different on each of the systems I've tried the game on.

I was on vacation last week, so the first laptop I tried the game on was my Razer Blade 16, with an RTX 5090 and a Ryzen AI 9 HX 370. It got a decent average frame rate at 1600p, but it was plagued with microstutters, especially in cutscenes. I started getting driver crashes, where the game would just make my laptop restart whenever I tried to load the game up — something that doesn't happen with any other game right now.
points: We got off to such a great start this year, with a ton of PC games that looked great and still ran well on pretty much any hardware.

highlights.title: Is a $1,000 pillow really better? The expensive pursuit of comfortable sleep
highlights.summary: From ergonomic memory foam to luxury goose down, Australia’s options for where to lay your head are enough to make it spin. So how do you choose the perfect pillow? The room inside Hästens’s “sleep spa” is calming.
body: It feels less like shopping and more like checking into a boutique hotel. The luxury brand, which has showrooms in Sydney and Melbourne, has celebrity fans, too. Emily Blunt loves her Hästens pillow so much she gave one to Oppenheimer co-star Cillian Murphy.
But what, exactly, makes a pillow worthy of such devotion? After years hunched over a laptop, plus occasional insomnia and many pillows of my own, I’m hoping to find out.

Sleep specialist Emilia Axelsson watches as I roll on to my side before sliding one pillow from beneath my head and replacing it with another. “This one’s too high,” she says, noticing my chin tip towards my chest. “When a pillow is the wrong height, your muscles work all night to hold your neck in position. The right pillow lets them switch off.”

Based on my fitting, Axelsson recommends two options: the Beddoc Therapeutic Pillow ($1,035), which combines down and feathers with an ergonomic core, and the Hästens High Firm Pillow ($725), a lofty down pillow for side sleepers who need more height.
points: From ergonomic memory foam to luxury goose down, Australia’s options for where to lay your head are enough to make it spin.

“Most Xbox One and Xbox Series X disc-based games support this new feature,” explains Jason Ronald, VP of next generation at Xbox. “Players can claim a digital entitlement by inserting a supported disc into an Xbox One or Xbox Series X console and launching the game.” This digital entitlement is tied to the specific disc, and it will move from account to account if you swap the physical game with a friend or log in to a different Xbox profile and try to play a disc-based game.

Microsoft will start testing this new Xbox disc-to-digital feature with Xbox Insider testers on August 31st, followed by a broader rollout to Xbox One and Xbox Series X consoles in the coming months. Once you have a digital version of an Xbox disc game, if supported you’ll also be able to access the game on PC through Xbox Play Anywhere, or stream it to multiple devices with Xbox Cloud Gaming.

highlights.title: AI models flub these intelligence tests. Can you fare any better?
highlights.summary: Puzzles and games have been central to AI development since the very beginning. Just as we humans like to test our smarts with crosswords or logic puzzles, developers can test how far models have advanced with a gaming gauntlet.
body: Judged purely on its puzzling skills, AI is improving a lot—and quickly. In late 2024, a team of scientists from Columbia University showed that even the best models could figure out only 18% of the infamous New York Times Connections puzzles; by early 2025, some models could solve them near perfectly every time.

But puzzles do more than just highlight the inexorable advance of AI capabilities. Seeing where models succeed and fail—and where we humans still beat them—can provide a useful window into the technology’s strengths and weaknesses. Despite advances, today’s models still fumble: Subtle changes in classic riddles often trip them up, and visual puzzles are a particular weak spot.

Here you’ll have the chance to test your wits on puzzles that have stumped models at one time or another. Some might be as tricky for you as they were for the AI; others are so simple that they’ll have you doubting whether AI is really intelligent at all. Each one highlights at least one way in which machine and human cognition differ. If you ace the test, you’ll have proved that you can out-puzzle an AI—at least for now.

highlights.title: ‘It was the hardcore equivalent of being a Deadhead’: consciousness-raising punk movement Krishnacore returns
highlights.summary: First-wave punks rejected religion – but come the 90s, bands embracing eastern thought found legions of devotees. Ahead of reformations and reissues, they discuss the Bhagavad Gita, brawls and tulasi beads in the pit.
body: Whether wielded as shock tactic or part of a considered philosophical stance, mockery and distrust of religion have been baked into punk rock’s DNA from the get-go. The Damned, Crass, the Germs and the Dead Kennedys all proffered early potshots and takedowns, and if Bad Brains received a grudging pass for their Rastafari leanings, in general, songs kowtowing to gods or masters were about as likely to win you scene cred as praise for Reagan, cops or nuclear war.

As the 80s ticked into the 90s, however, something curious began to happen: a clutch of bands emerged who were wise to the hardcore classicism of Minor Threat and SSD but also looked east to Krishna consciousness. Leading the way was Ray “Raghunath” Cappo who, barely into his 20s, had already broken down walls as frontman for Youth of Today, a New York band who combined a straight-edge philosophy with animal-rights advocacy and a sense of full-throated positivity. He and guitarist John Porcelly had “witnessed enough young people screwing up their lives that we thought, as simple as it is, it’s a positive message. Let’s rally behind it,” he says. “And it became big, bigger than we expected.”
